messages:
Maria Lo: Heads up — saw a big spike in dashboard main bundle size and a correlated slowdown in chart paints on Canary after yesterday's routing policy change. Charts hang ~400–800ms longer on first interaction.
Jon Patel: saw perf alerts too, good catch. Any specific route or dataset that reproduces?
Maria Lo: heatmap + time-series panels on project /usage/2024 seem worst. Local repro steps: open dashboard, select 90d range, hover a series -> main thread spikes and chunks parse.
Lee Chen: interesting — our bundle delta shows +180KB to main ~gzipped. That could trigger more parse work. Could be the new splitpoint placement rolled in?
Ashley R: I pushed the splitpoint tweak in the route optimizer PR, it moved embedlib -> inline to reduce network requests. Maybe backfired with the new telemetry shim.
Jon Patel: can you paste the asset map? Also any console telemetry import changes?
Ashley R: paste: ```json
{"main.js": "main.a1b2c3.js", "embedlib.js": "embed.4d5e6f.js", "telemetry.js": "tele.7g8h9i.js"}
```
Maria Lo: telemetry import changed to eager init for sampling, per the rollout note. I wonder if that increases main parse work due to closure allocation.
Samir (deploy-bot): Canary deploy 2024-11-11T03:12:45 completed — rollouts: route-optimizer-v2 on 10% of traffic.
Lee Chen: timeline aligns. Two hypotheses: 1) moved code into main increased parse time; 2) prefetch/backpressure interaction — prefetch triggers now queue more work on main thread instead of worker.
Jon Patel: I can reproduce locally when I enable eager telemetry + inline embedlib. If I toggle telemetry to lazy load, charts recover.
Ashley R: ok i'll rollback inline embedlib for Canary and flip telemetry back to deferred for the canary bucket. Quick patch: change import to `const telemetry = lazy(() => import('./telemetry'))` and keep embedlib as separate chunk.
Maria Lo: patch looks good. Suggest we also add a short-term mitigation: add a small debounce before first hover renders to avoid parse storm when users open multiple panels.
Lee Chen: agree. Also let's run a flamegraph on the canary JS to see parse/compile hotspots. Jon, can you collect perf.trace from the canary session?
Jon Patel: uploading trace now -> https://artifacts.internal/traces/1734506789/trace-1.zip
Maria Lo: saw two hot spots: telemetry init (~35% CPU during first paint) and a new object-map reducer in main (~25%). The reducer came from the splitpoint change, it merged a tiny util that was previously in embedlib.
Ashley R: merging that util seemed harmless but combined with eager telemetry it pushes parsing over the threshold. Rolling back inline and reverting telemetry to lazy should fix. I'll send the revert PR now.
Samir (deploy-bot): PR 4821 opened by Ashley R: revert(inline-embedlib, eager-telemetry). Auto CI triggered.
Jon Patel: after applying the revert locally perf returns to baseline (~<60ms added paint). Good.
Lee Chen: next steps: 1) revert on Canary and monitor LCP and interactive metrics; 2) add automated bundle-delta guardrail in CI to block >100KB gzipped additions without a flag; 3) add an entry to rollout checklist to run local main-thread flamecheck if moving splitpoints.
Maria Lo: +1 on the checklist and the CI gate. Also add a `telemetry.lazyInit` feature flag we can toggle without deploy.
Ashley R: SG — will follow up with PRs for the gate + feature flag after the revert lands.
Jon Patel: monitoring: I'll watch SLO dashboards and open a postmortem if regression persists.
Maria Lo: thanks everyone. Quick note: users hitting the canary showed gravatar images loading too — not related but added work on paint. We'll keep an eye. :thumbsup:
Ashley R: revert merged to Canary at 03:45, Samir?
Samir (deploy-bot): Canary deploy 2024-11-11T03:46:02 completed — route-optimizer-v2 at 5% now with revert. No errors reported.
Jon Patel: early metrics look good, chart p95 paint dropped back to baseline in the canary bucket.
Maria Lo: marking this thread resolved — follow-ups assigned to Ashley (CI gate + flag) and Lee (flamegraph infra).
Ashley R: on it.
Lee Chen: will add flamegraph automation.
Maria Lo: closing.
